translationRepairs: Is this not the superfluous flourish of the Two Emperors and Three Kings!
Surely this is no mere superfluous flourish of the Two Emperors and Three Kings!
豈…哉 is a rhetorical denial: ritual-music is not the Two Emperors and Three Kings' mere ornamental excess. English “Is this not…” affirms the opposite polarity.

Earlier, in the Zhenglong period, Prince Hailing built the Imperial Ancestral Temple at Bian; when Zhenyou moved south, Emperor Xuanzong repaired it to enshrine the spirit tablets of the various emperors.

Earlier, in the Zhenglong period, Prince Hailing built the Imperial Ancestral Temple at Bian; when the court moved south in the Zhenyou period, Emperor Xuanzong repaired it to enshrine the spirit tablets of the various emperors.
貞祐 is the Zhenyou era; 南遷 is the court's southward move. The original makes Zhenyou the mover.
The music used at the separate temples of Empress Zhaode and the Filial and Cultivated Crown Prince is recorded in the ritual protocols and hymn texts.
The music used at the separate temples of Empress Zhaode and Crown Prince Xuanxiao is recorded in the ritual protocols and hymn texts.
宣孝太子 is the posthumous title Crown Prince Xuanxiao, not a pair of English epithets “Filial and Cultivated.”
